questions.q: Which Cypher clause behaves as the direct equivalent of T-SQL's TOP?
options: LIMIT
WHERE
MERGE
collect()
questions.explain: LIMIT caps the number of result rows returned, the same job TOP does in T-SQL.

questions.q: What makes collect() distinctly graph/document-flavored compared to standard SQL aggregates like COUNT and AVG?
options: It gathers matched values into a list on a single result row, which fits naturally with Cypher's document-shaped results rather than strictly tabular ones
It only works on relationship properties, never on node properties
It is identical to SQL's GROUP_CONCAT and works exactly the same way
It can only be used inside a WHERE clause
questions.explain: collect() aggregates values into a list, an idiomatic pattern because Cypher results aren't forced into strict tabular rows the way SQL results are.

questions.q: How does Cypher determine the grouping key when a RETURN clause mixes a plain field with aggregate functions, e.g. RETURN c.name, count(p)?
options: Any non-aggregated field in the RETURN list becomes the implicit grouping key — there is no GROUP BY clause in Cypher
Cypher requires an explicit GROUP BY clause, just like T-SQL, or the query fails
Cypher groups by the first matched node's internal ID automatically, ignoring RETURN fields
Grouping is undefined and the result order is random
questions.explain: Cypher has no GROUP BY clause; any non-aggregated field returned becomes the implicit grouping key, and this is always unambiguous.

questions.q: In Cypher, when is a WHERE clause evaluated relative to MATCH?
options: After MATCH finds candidate patterns, keeping only the ones meeting the condition
Before MATCH runs, to pre-filter the entire database
WHERE cannot be used together with MATCH in the same query
WHERE only applies to relationship types, never to node properties
questions.explain: WHERE filters the rows MATCH has already found, the same evaluation order as SQL Server's WHERE clause on a FROM/JOIN result.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid WHERE condition on a relationship property in Cypher, assuming r is a bound relationship variable?
options: WHERE r.since > 2019
WHERE RELATIONSHIP(r) > 2019
Relationship properties cannot be filtered in Cypher, only node properties
WHERE r::since > 2019
questions.explain: Relationships can carry properties just like nodes, and they're filtered with the same dot-property syntax, e.g. r.since > 2019.
